done_when: forge close runs the repo's test command on the machine it runs on and gives the reviewer the result, listing what passed and what was skipped with the reason; the review brief says a skipped test that the close run passed is not a missing test, and that for a pure deletion a test showing the old input is now refused is enough; tests run forge close with a test command that passes and one that skips

findings.body: Forge's default Go test command is `go test ./...` (`src/forge/init.py:55`). This new call runs that command unchanged. In package-list mode, Go prints only an `ok` summary for a passing package unless `-v` is set, so a skipped test and its reason never reach the output filter. This is evidence the earlier generic-summary ruling did not account for: the reviewer can see that the package passed, but cannot see what was skipped or why. See the [Go command documentation](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go).
findings.title: Not done: forge close reports skipped Go tests with reasons

findings.body: The new Go-style test runs `gotest.py`, which prints canned `--- SKIP` and reason lines. It never runs Forge's supported `go test ./...` command (`src/forge/init.py:55`), so it passes while the Go skip-reporting defect remains. This is new evidence relative to the earlier finding about pytest-only coverage: the added case still cannot fail when real Go skips disappear. Exercise `forge close` with an actual skipped Go test and assert that its reason reaches the review brief.
findings.title: Not done: a forge close test proves skipped Go tests reach the reviewer

findings.body: The revised cap still drops the middle of the selected output when it exceeds 80 lines. For example, a pytest `-rs` summary with 100 skipped tests can lose skip entries and their reasons while retaining the final skipped count. That leaves the reviewer without the promised reason for every listed skip.
findings.title: Preserve skip reasons beyond the 80-line cap

why: Reviewers can't see tests that only run outside the worker's sandbox, such as database tests, so every database change is flagged as untested even when those tests pass
